memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned: Bela son of Beor became king of Edom. His city was named Dinhabah. When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him as king. When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him as king. When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, succeeded him as king. His city was named Avith. When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him as king. When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river succeeded him as king. When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Akbor succeeded him as king. When Baal-Hanan son of Akbor died, Hadad succeeded him as king. His city was named Pau, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-Zahab." - Gen 36:31-39 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Edom had kings early — even "before any Israelite king reigned." But read this list carefully and one phrase repeats like a solemn drumbeat: "When Bela died... when Jobab died... when Husham died..." One king after another rises to power, reigns for a time, and then dies, giving way to the next. Crown after crown passes from one head to another, and every reign ends the same way — in a grave.

This is the story of all earthly power. However great a ruler, however grand his city, death has the final word over every human throne. The most powerful king is still mortal. Kingdoms rise and fall, and their kings die and are replaced. Human glory is real, but it is always temporary.

Against this backdrop, the Bible points us to a different kind of King. From the line of Jacob, in time, would come Israel's kings — and ultimately Jesus, of whom the angel said, "he will reign... forever, and his kingdom will never end" (Luke 1:33). Unlike the kings of Edom, this King "always lives" (Heb 7:25). Death has no claim on Him, for He rose from the grave.

Where do you place your hope — in the passing powers of this world, or in the King who never dies? Every earthly crown will fall. Only the kingdom of Christ endures forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I tempted to put my hope in passing earthly powers?
2. How does the eternal reign of Christ steady my heart?
3. What does it mean to belong to a kingdom that never ends?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, earthly kings rise and die, but You reign forever and Your kingdom has no end. I place my hope in You, the King who lives forever. Let me belong wholly to Your unending kingdom. Amen.
